payload.rationale: The YES event requires a published single-decimal monthly CPI increase of 0.3% or higher; a reported 0.2% does not qualify. Under ordinary rounding, the effective threshold is approximately 0.25% before rounding. Interpreting the contract as the standard headline month-over-month CPI measure, I assign a 45% chance based on general background knowledge: monthly inflation commonly lies near this boundary, while energy prices and other volatile components can move the headline figure substantially. This is a background-rate judgment, not a forecast supported by current 2026 observations. The strongest reason the estimate could be too high is that sustained disinflation, weaker demand, or falling energy prices could put November's underlying monthly rate comfortably below the threshold. The strongest reason it could be too low is that persistent services inflation or an energy-price surge could make a rounded increase of at least 0.3% more likely than not.
limitations: No current research, inflation releases, energy-price observations, or other contemporaneous evidence was supplied.
The estimate assumes the standard headline monthly CPI measure; the excerpt does not explicitly specify seasonal adjustment or the precise series.
The forecast concerns November 2026 inflation as published under the contract's rules, not year-over-year inflation or an unrounded increase strictly above 0.2%.
Without current conditions, the probability has substantial uncertainty.
